05-1.title: Chatbot vs agent
05-1.tldr: A chatbot maps one input to one model reply; an agent runs a loop (model → tools → results → repeat) until a stopping condition.
points: Chatbot: one model turn, no tools.
Agent: tool/reason loop with a stopping rule.
The loop and tools, not the model, define an agent.

05-2.title: Workflow vs agent
05-2.tldr: A workflow is a pre-declared graph (you author steps/edges/branches); an agent decides its next step at runtime from model output.
points: Agent: runtime branching on model output.
A workflow can embed an agent as a node.

05-3.title: Linear chain vs conditional graph
05-3.tldr: A linear chain always activates the next step; a graph adds routing (choose successors from state) and joining/barriers (when a merge node is ready).
points: Graph: conditional edges route by state.

05-4.title: ReAct pattern
05-4.tldr: ReAct alternates thought → action → observation, so each tool result informs the next reasoning step.
points: Each observation feeds the next thought.
Repeats until there are no tool calls.

05-5.title: Why interleave reasoning and actions
05-5.tldr: A fully upfront plan cannot react to what tools return; interleaving feeds each result back so the agent adapts.
points: An upfront plan executes with no feedback.
Interleaving grounds each step in real results.
Adapts when reality differs from the plan.

05-6.title: Hard iteration limit
05-6.tldr: Cap the loop with a max-iteration/round counter plus token/time budgets, enforced (not just reported), with a cap at each nesting level and configurable.
points: Cap each nested loop; make caps configurable.

05-7.title: What stops an agent
05-7.tldr: Usually the model: no tool calls means the answer is final. Around that sit hard limits — max iterations, token/time budgets, explicit stop conditions.
points: Outer loop: stop evaluators + completion promise.

05-8.title: Infinite tool-calling loop
05-8.tldr: Cap iterations, detect repetition on canonicalized (tool,args), nudge or abort on no progress, and cap rounds/tokens/time.

05-9.title: 'The agent is stuck': tests shipped experience
05-9.tldr: 'The agent is stuck' tests whether you've shipped one, not studied one.

05-10.title: 'Stuck in a loop': production experience
05-10.tldr: 'The agent is stuck in a loop' is testing production experience.
